parsed.explanation: No criminalisation or documented universal facility/border ban, and courts have ordered release, awarded HRT-denial damages, annulled anti-LGBT resolutions and recognised non-binary discrimination. Against that, a trans foreign national was placed in a male guarded centre with three months' HRT interruption, hate-crime law does not cover gender identity after veto/unconstitutional amendments, and documented hostility includes LGBT-free zones, hostile head-of-state rhetoric and a violent 2019 counter-protest. Combined regime is therefore materially below strong-protection anchors but above routine-detention regimes.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented trans-specific border refusal; visa-free 90 days noted. Document practice under civil-status/identity laws examined for residents, not shown applied to visitors.
entry_documents.protection: Visa-free entry documented; no barrier documented for foreign passports.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch could lead to detention, as in custody case, but dossier does not document routine entry friction.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: March 2024: court placed trans foreign national in guarded centre for male foreigners; centre refused HRT for three months. July 2024: prison authorities denied trans prisoner HRT.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Border commander ordered release after NGO intervention; human-rights court awarded EUR 8,000 for HRT denial, showing litigation can succeed.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Birth-sex placement creates custody harm; remedies arrive after harm and depend on NGO/legal intervention.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No bathroom, ward, shelter or public-facility exclusion rule for visitors documented. Residual family-rights charters and annulled LGBT-free resolutions are local discriminatory acts, not documented facility bans.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Administrative courts held anti-LGBT resolutions exceeded powers and unconstitutional; last explicit resolution annulled Feb 2024.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local hostile acts persist in 11 places, but no documented universal facility exposure for travellers.

care_services.exposure: Guarded centre refused hormone supply for three months in 2024 case; most recent documented instance is March 2024, recurrence since not documented.
care_services.protection: Human-rights court found HRT denial violated Convention rights and ordered damages, establishing enforceable precedent.
care_services.interaction: Care denial occurs in detention; community/emergency care access for visitors not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Same-sex conduct decriminalised since 1932/1948, no trans-specific criminal offence documented. Head of state hostile rhetoric 2020; 2021 rally branding LGBT enemies; LGBT-free zones 2019-23.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No criminalisation; Prosecutor General special response team/guidelines noted, but hate-speech/hate-crime extension postponed/vetoed/ruled unconstitutional, not in force for gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official hostility coexists with courts annulling discriminatory resolutions; enforcement protection against gender-identity hate crime is absent.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No visitor-facing minor, school, custody or family-travel rule specific to trans visitors documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Resident adoption/IVF/partnership restrictions do not document a traveller-facing minor exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: July 2019 equality march: 800 marchers confronted by 4,000+ counter-protesters throwing stones/bricks/firecrackers, heavy riot police needed; Aug 2020 47 arrested at protest; travel advisory lists harassment motives including appearance/sexual orientation; 2025 report of tech-facilitated gender-based violence.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Riot police intervened in 2019; Ombudsman criticised 2020 mass arrest, but no documented hate-crime prosecution for gender identity as qualifying motive.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Event-scoped and dated violence plus ongoing online abuse, with thin gender-identity-specific recourse, creates tier-3 hostility risk.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Hate-crime/hate-speech law excludes gender identity/sexual orientation; March 2025 amendments never entered force after veto and Sept 2025 unconstitutional ruling.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have worked for trans claimants: release, HRT damages, annulment of resolutions, Feb 2025 non-binary discrimination recognition.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Judicial recourse is real but retrospective; it does not pre-empt custody placement, HRT interruption or street harassment.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in that brief detention ended with release and courts/apology/damages remedied harm, but here placement was in a male guarded centre with three months HRT interruption, more severe, so rating is below 0.65.

Higher than 0.55 ward-by-marker regime because no documented universal facility or registration rule applies to every visitor; exposure is principally custody-if-detained and hostile street climate, with some judicial remedy.

Lower than 0.75 because hate-crime protection for gender identity is not in force, top-level hostility and LGBT-free legacy are documented, and the custody/HRT case shows state-imposed harm not pre-empted by protections.

parsed.synthesis: Combined operative regime: no criminalisation, no documented universal entry/facility ban, and functioning courts that release, compensate and annul discriminatory acts. However, if stopped or detained a visitor faces birth-sex male-centre placement and documented HRT refusal, remedy only after NGO/litigation harm; in public, gender-identity hate crime has no qualifying protection after veto, amid documented hostility and event violence. That interaction places the case at the reduced/elevated boundary, below working-protection anchors and above routine administrative-exposure regimes.
